$schema.description: The JSON Schema editors complete and validate this config against. ocel init writes it.

allowDegraded.description: The needs this project waives rather than have a deploy refused over.

apps.description: The apps this project deploys. Left off, ocel detects one at the project root.

arch.description: The processor architecture an app's functions or container image are built for. Left off, what the provider runs the app on.

buildWithResources.description: Whether ocel deploy lets the app's build reach the resources it uses in the deployed environment, so a page prerendered at build time reads them. Only a Next app's build reaches them, on serverless or container compute: its postgres databases and kv stores over ports the provider forwards, and its buckets through the binding proxy the provider serves. Any other build goes without. Left off, true. Set false to build as if no resource were provisioned.

allOf.description: What the app runs on: serverless functions packed per route, or one container image serving everything. Named alone, or keyed by the compute with its options as the value.

serverless.description: Serverless functions packed per route, which scale themselves.

entrypoint.description: The file a node app is served from, or the directory of a go app's main package, when it is not the one ocel would detect.

framework.description: What the app is built with, when ocel is not to read it off the app's own manifest.

serverless.title: ServerlessCompute

container.description: One container image serving every route.

health.description: How the app is checked before it is served.

path.description: The path the check requests, off the app's own root. Any 2xx answer means up. Left off, a VPS finds the path by probing /up, /health, /healthz and / in turn and keeps the first that exists, and AWS and Google Cloud request /.

health.title: HealthConfig

image.description: How the app's image is built.

command.description: The command that builds the app inside the image. Left off, the app's own build script runs.

context.description: The directory the image is built from, relative to the project. Left off, it is the workspace root the app belongs to.

dockerfile.description: The Dockerfile to build from. A relative path resolves against the app's directory.

image.title: ImageConfig

instances.description: How many instances of the app run.

max.description: The most instances run at once, however busy the app is. Left off, as many as min, or 1.

min.description: The fewest instances kept running, however quiet the app is. Left off, 1.

instances.title: InstancesConfig

container.title: ContainerCompute

allOf.title: ComputeDescriptor

compute.description: What the app runs on, keyed by the compute with its options as the value, or named alone. Left off, the first compute the provider runs.

domains.description: The hostnames this app is served on.

production.description: The hostnames production is served on.

domains.title: AppDomainConfig

folder.description: The variables folder this app reads, when it does not read the project's own.

name.description: The app's name. It is a label of every resource the app deploys and of its preview hostname, so it is a DNS label.

path.description: The app's directory, relative to the config.

bindings.description: Resources this project declares that ocel binds instead of provisioning them itself. Keyed by resource type, then by the name the app declares. The value is "@" followed by the name a record your own infrastructure published, such as "@warehouse", and a name nothing has published refuses the deploy; or the record written inline, checked at deploy rather than provisioned, optionally keyed by the tier it serves.

host.description: The base URL of a self-hosted Infisical. Left off, https://app.infisical.com.

path.description: The Infisical folder the project's values sit under. A variables folder such as /web reads from that folder beneath it. Left off, the environment's root, /.

project.description: The id of the Infisical project the values live in.

write.description: What ocel may write into Infisical. "missing" creates a key a declaration names and Infisical lacks, and never overwrites one. "values" also updates a value Infisical holds, from ocel env set or the variables page, unless it changed in Infisical since ocel last read it. Nothing ocel does ever deletes a key there. Left off, "never". Refused for dev, which only reads.

allOf.title: InfisicalOptions

infisical.description: Infisical, read as the machine identity auth names and synced every minute.

allOf.title: EnvSourceDescriptor

production.description: Where production's values are read from. Left off, ocel's own store in your account ("builtin").

envSource.title: EnvSourceConfig

lifecycle.description: Commands ocel runs on this machine at points of a deploy.

preBuild.description: Runs once per deploy, after the project's infrastructure is provisioned and before any app is built, with the bindings of the deployed environment. A non-zero exit or a timeout stops the deploy before it builds anything, and nothing is promoted. Written as the command alone, or as an object.

oneOf.description: A shell command ocel runs on this machine with the bindings of the deployed environment, and where, when and for how long it runs.

app.description: The app whose variables the command also receives, and whose directory it runs from. Left off, the command gets the bindings alone and runs from the project directory.

command.description: The shell command to run, from the project directory, or from the app's directory when app is set.

previews.description: Which previews run the command: persistent previews, which have infrastructure of their own, all previews, or none. Production always runs it. Left off, persistent: an ephemeral preview gets no infrastructure of its own and shares the preview tier's databases, so a migration there would change what every other ephemeral preview reads.

timeout.description: How long the command may run, as a duration such as 90s or 15m, before it is stopped and the deploy fails. Left off, 30m.

oneOf.title: LifecycleCommand

lifecycle.title: LifecycleConfig

provider.description: The provider ocel deploy provisions into, keyed by its identifier with its options as the value. Its options also name the edge in front of the origin and the DNS service hostname records are written into. A provider that needs no options may be named alone.

dns.description: Where the project's hostname records are written, keyed by the DNS service's identifier with its options as the value, or named alone.

zone.description: The zone the records are written into. Omit it and ocel picks the zone that covers the hostname.

dns.title: DNSDescriptor

edge.description: The edge in front of the origin, keyed by its identifier with its options as the value, or named alone. Omit it for the provider's default: CloudFront on AWS, and no edge on GCP or a VPS.
edge.title: EdgeDescriptor

provider.title: ProviderDescriptor

registry.description: Where this project's container images are pushed.

password.description: The environment variable containing the password or token, written as "${REGISTRY_TOKEN}" and read where the push authenticates — never the secret itself.

server.description: The registry host and the namespace images sit under, such as ghcr.io/acme. No scheme, and no credentials.

username.description: The username the push authenticates as, where the registry wants one.

registry.title: RegistryConfig

slug.description: The project's deployment identity. Every stack and resource ocel creates in your own account is keyed on it, so changing it forks a new project.

transforms.description: Transform modules applied while provisioning, in order — later modules win where their patches collide. Each is a path to a module whose default export is a defineTransform(...) result, keyed by the provider it patches.
